title: Commodity hedging
subtitle: Weekly note for corporate hedging conversations: energy, metals, grains
headline: Week of 04 November 2026. Backwardation in Brent Crude, WTI Crude, Aluminium; contango in Natural Gas, Copper, Gold, Wheat, Corn. Realized vol is high against five years in Brent Crude, Gold, Silver and low in Natural Gas, Wheat, Corn, Soybeans: that is where option hedges are dear and cheap.

sections.title: Energy: what a hedge locks in, and what optionality costs
paragraphs: Brent Crude: backwardation, BZZ27 17.6% below BZF27. A producer selling 11 months forward locks in 17.6% less than the front; a consumer buying forward pays 17.6% less.
WTI Crude: backwardation, CLZ27 17.0% below CLZ26. A producer selling 12 months forward locks in 17.0% less than the front; a consumer buying forward pays 17.0% less.
Natural Gas: contango, NGZ27 35.1% above NGZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 35.1% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 35.1% more.

Brent Crude: realized vol 51%, 87th percentile of five years. Options-based hedges (puts, collars) are expensive against history; forwards and swaps carry no vol premium. WTI Crude: realized vol 46%, 77th percentile of five years, in line with history. Implied vol, which is what an option actually costs, is 62%: well above what has been realized (+15.8 points). Natural Gas: realized vol 49%, 17th percentile of five years. Optionality is cheap against history: the moment to price puts, collars or participating forwards.

sections.title: Metals: what a hedge locks in, and what optionality costs
paragraphs: Copper: contango, HGZ27 4.6% above HGZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 4.6% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 4.6% more.

Aluminium: backwardation, ALIM27 3.9% below ALIZ26. A producer selling 6 months (the furthest contract on the free feed) forward locks in 3.9% less than the front; a consumer buying forward pays 3.9% less.
Gold: contango, GCZ27 5.0% above GCZ26. A consumer buying 12 months forward pays 5.0% more than the front; a producer selling forward locks in 5.0% more.
Silver: flat curve, SIZ27 within 0.7% of SIZ26: forward hedges lock in roughly today's price.

Copper: realized vol 22%, 38th percentile of five years, in line with history. Aluminium: realized vol 22%, 47th percentile of five years, in line with history. Gold: realized vol 22%, 84th percentile of five years. Options-based hedges (puts, collars) are expensive against history; forwards and swaps carry no vol premium. Implied vol, which is what an option actually costs, is 26%: close to what has been realized (+3.3 points). Silver: realized vol 45%, 83rd percentile of five years. Options-based hedges (puts, collars) are expensive against history; forwards and swaps carry no vol premium.

method: Talking points rank markets by how far their 12-month curve or their realized-vol percentile sits from normal. Context for client conversations, not a recommendation.
caveats: Free data: Yahoo Finance closes of NYMEX, COMEX and CBOT futures. Copper and aluminium are COMEX contracts, not LME; Brent is the NYMEX last-day financial contract. No TTF, power, coal, softs or pulp on the free feed.
Implied vol history exists only for WTI (OVX) and gold (GVZ). Elsewhere the realized-vol percentile stands in for what options cost, which holds only if implied tracks realized.
The front-month series rolls from contract to contract, so weekly and monthly moves include roll gaps.

Curves come from listed contracts only (12 to 13 months out, fewer for grains and aluminium), not from swap curves. Deferred metal contracts trade thinly, so intermediate points can be noisy; the 12-month comparison uses the same delivery month a year later, usually the most liquid.
